en.title: NTSB says Florida Learjet 60 showed signs of breaking up before impact
en.summary: The NTSB says there is evidence a Learjet 60 that crashed near West Palm Beach, Florida, began breaking up before impact, killing all nine people on board, while investigators have not yet identified which components separated.
body: The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) says investigators have found evidence that a Learjet 60 began breaking up before it crashed near West Palm Beach, Florida, on November 1, 2026, killing all nine people on board. Board Member Tom Chapman said at a briefing on November 2: "We do have some evidence that there was some breakup of the aircraft before impact." He did not confirm which components, if any, had separated, and said investigators were still seeking to determine that. Investigators have identified debris beyond the main crash site, and Chapman asked members of the public who find aircraft parts not to move them but to contact the NTSB or local authorities.

The aircraft was operated by Aurora Aviation, doing business as Upper Jets, on a Part 135 charter flight. It departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (AUS) at 09:37 local time for North Eleuthera in the Bahamas, carrying two pilots and seven passengers, and crashed at approximately 12:51 local time; one man in a vehicle on the ground suffered a leg injury. At approximately 12:47 local time, a pilot reported light clear ice that was manageable along with moderate turbulence at 35,000 feet, with altitude deviations of about 700 feet. After reporting precipitation, the crew requested a climb to 37,000 feet, which air traffic control approved, but less than 30 seconds later the crew reported the aircraft was descending, declared a mayday, and reported descent rates reaching 20,000 feet per minute before communications were lost. Chapman said weather conditions are a major focus of the investigation, and investigators planned to examine weather and air traffic control communications. The aircraft was listed as carrying a cockpit voice recorder that had not yet been recovered, and water filling the impact crater was hampering access to the main wreckage.

facts.claim: NTSB investigators found evidence that a Learjet 60 shed some components before crashing near West Palm Beach, Florida, killing all nine people on board on November 1, 2026.
At a November 2 briefing, NTSB Board Member Tom Chapman said: "We do have some evidence that there was some breakup of the aircraft before impact," without confirming which components separated.
Investigators have identified debris beyond the main crash site, and Chapman asked the public not to move any aircraft parts found but to contact the NTSB or local authorities.
The Upper Jets Part 135 charter departed Austin-Bergstrom at 09:37 local time for North Eleuthera with two pilots and seven passengers and crashed at approximately 12:51 local time.

At about 12:47 local time the crew reported light clear ice and moderate turbulence at 35,000 feet, then requested a climb to 37,000 feet; less than 30 seconds after clearance, the crew reported a descent, declared a mayday, and reported descent rates reaching 20,000 feet per minute.
Chapman said weather conditions are a major focus of the investigation, and the cockpit voice recorder had not yet been recovered.

zh.title: NTSB：佛羅里達Learjet60墜毀前已有空中解體跡證
zh.summary: 美國國家運輸安全委員會表示，佛羅里達Learjet60墜機事故已有飛機在撞擊前解體的跡證，但尚未確認是哪個部件脫落，天氣仍是調查重點。
body: 美國國家運輸安全委員會（NTSB）表示，11月1日在佛羅里達州西棕櫚灘附近墜毀的Learjet60，在撞擊地面之前已有部分解體的跡證，機上9人全部罹難。委員會委員查普曼在11月2日的簡報中說：「We do have some evidence that there was some breakup of the aircraft before impact.」，但他沒有確認是哪個部件脫落，也表示調查人員仍在確認相關細節。調查人員已在主殘骸場之外發現碎片，並呼籲民眾若發現飛機殘骸不要移動，應聯繫調查單位或當地機關。

這架由Upper Jets營運的Part135包機，於當地時間上午9時37分自奧斯汀伯格斯特羅姆國際機場起飛，目的地是巴哈馬北伊柳塞拉，機上有2名機組員與7名乘客，約在中午12時51分墜毀，地面一名車內男子腿部受傷。約在中午12時47分，機組回報在35,000英尺高度遇到可應付的輕微結冰與中度亂流，隨後因降水請求爬升至37,000英尺並獲准，但在獲准不到30秒後就回報飛機正在下降並發出求救訊號，下降率一度達到每分鐘20,000英尺，隨後失去聯繫。查普曼表示，天氣狀況是調查的一大重點，調查人員將檢視航路天氣與航管通訊，機上的座艙語音紀錄器尚未尋獲，而撞擊坑積水也影響了主要殘骸的回收工作。
